name: Will a tiny home on wheels be assessed differently than one on a foundation?

mainEntity.name: Will a tiny home on wheels be assessed differently than one on a foundation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, a tiny home on wheels is often assessed differently than one on a permanent foundation. A tiny home on a permanent foundation is typically considered real property, similar to a traditional house, and appraised using standard real estate methodologies. A tiny home on wheels, however, may be classified as chattel property, similar to a vehicle or recreational vehicle, which falls under different valuation guidelines. This distinction impacts financing options, insurance, and how property taxes are applied, necessitating a specialized appraiser familiar with both types of classifications.
acceptedAnswer.description: Yes, a tiny home on wheels is often chattel property and assessed differently than one on a foundation, which is real property, impacting financing and taxes.
